touches.text: Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).

A rule not yet enforced is made into a ticket now, never left floating as prose. So ticket f5dbfddea8c6 makes the rewrites it proposed at the remaining sites (the press office, PROOF.md). Where a site names a rule whose physics is not built, it names that rule's real ticket id, cast now if none exists; the word "ticket" with no id behind it does not count. - CC

CLAUDE.md and MAP.md are not edited site by site: CLAUDE.md is rewritten from these pieces (10.3.11) and MAP.md dissolves, so neither carries the word after that. The three rules CLAUDE.md still lists as gaps (relational state, the derived lab, history reach) are built (inspector.py, compiler.py verify_lab), so the rewrite drops them. CC's decision, Q#117 and Q#118. - CC

Skills (skills/: cairnhelp, challenge, chart, commit, intent, sorted, ...) are Claude Code's. The deterministic parts move out of markdown into CC device verbs: a skill's OS-side work runs as a script, and CC's shim processes the result and injects it into the session. WHY: every habit captured that way is one CC no longer spends inference on, so CC gets faster; a first charting pass done in deterministic Python with no LLM until after saved about 90% of tokens, measured in real use.

CLAUDE.md is the first file every CC session reads: the Laws, pointers into these files, and the rules still in prose, each a bug with its ticket. About 2k tokens, and challenged at every addition. WHY: it loads into every turn, so every word costs every session.
A rule CLAUDE.md names that is still prose is a bug with a ticket. WHY: unenforced rules used to pile up, so a law now forbids them; any that stands is a bug. -amm

A line without "-amm" is not his call. When lines conflict, the by-lines are checked first. WHY: the by-line says whose call a line is, so an adjudication starts from who decided rather than re-deriving it.

QUESTIONS: a question is [Q#n: ...], placed at the line it bears on. Its #n is its own and never changes; a new one takes the next unused number, which is now 126. An answered question disappears: its answer is folded into the intention and why (0.2.1), and signed where it records a decision (0.5). Why? Becuase too many words makes it hard for both akien and Claude to understand.

A choice CC can answer is not a question; it is a hypothesis. The ticket carries CC's answer as its hypothesis, and its WATCHME feeds the hypothesis back to cc_0 with enough data to review it and rewrite it as we learn. The notation carries the question: a HYPOTHESIS asks whether it works, or is faster, or whatever it claims, and the WATCHME answers that. A question asks only what Akien alone can settle. Why? Because a question with a recommendation asks him to adjudicate what a measurement can settle. This holds everywhere. - CC
Questions live here and nowhere else. The questions/ inbox and `cairn question` are deprecated for now. -amm

Every sieve carries its own why, and the why names where it came from. Akien designed the inspector tools; CC built each specific sieve from what it read him to mean. So the adjudication in 17.11.6 is against the sieve's own why, done by CC, and never a question to him. The sieves are not perfect and nothing here will be: the whole is always under improvement, and each sieve's why is what lets it be judged. Today build_inspector registers 43 sieves, and the 36 sieves/*.json records carry name, band and dials but no why. The whys live only in docstrings.

The same boundary runs wherever Akien designed a tool or machine and CC filled in its specific contents: the nest and its questions, the inspectors and their sieves, the gates and their checks, the corrosion set, the skill doors and their field lists. Each such component's charter carries a design_boundary naming what Akien designed, what CC designed, and how a red over CC's part is settled. CC's part is CC's to adjudicate against its own why. Akien may be asked whether a part could be better, with the whys laid out, and whatever CC can't sort goes to him. A new component that has this boundary declares it in its charter when it is born.

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.
